mechanism: Link an ordered lower/upper stripe pair in the step-one pentagon to the rising stripe pair in C. Targets extrapolating the shown 21-degree rising orientation to the nearest rising aligned-outline diagram, rather than finding the first allowed pentagon-symmetry multiple. The slopes are qualitatively rising but are not asserted equal.
mathematical_solution: A regular pentagon fills its fixed hole exactly at rotations divisible by 72 degrees. After n whole steps its rotation is 21n degrees, so 21n=72k. Dividing by 3 gives 7n=24k; hence the least positive n is 24 and the total rotation is 504 degrees, equivalent to 144 degrees. The initially horizontal paper lines then have undirected orientation 144 degrees (descending rightwards), which is B. The other option orientations are A72, C36, D108 and E0 degrees, all distinguishable from B144 modulo180. The given step-one lines have21degrees. Four colored existing stripes leave the polygon hole, all horizontal background lines and every option fully intact; no marked line is a new cut.
human_semantics: Only four existing stripe segments are recolored at 2pt. Lower/upper ordering gives both colors a role. No contour is recolored and no new partition or ink-continuity condition is given. Options remain distinguished by their unchanged actual stripe angles.

marker_roles.role: A lower interior stripe of the actual step-one rotated pentagon, serving as the lower feature in an ordered pair.
An upper interior stripe of the same actual pentagon; the pair carries the visible rising direction and order.
C lower rising stripe proposed as the first feature copy when the outline next fills the hole.
C upper rising stripe proposed as the companion feature copy; favors retaining rising line orientation rather than the required first closing rotation.
